cells.tense: You are here and the giving and receiving are landing evenly on both sides.
cells.act: set the finished thing down in a form that keeps
cells.ask: Put one arrangement the change left you — the split, the terms, what you now know — into a form that holds without your hand on it, and leave it alone this week.
cells.core:
The exchange between you and the other people in this runs both ways right now, and it runs that way because you let go of something first. What you released made room for giving to land, and receiving to follow. That is the harvest of something carried a long time and then put down.

The risk is the setting-down. What an ending released can drift if nobody keeps it — the new terms, the fair split, the thing you now know — so the next move is to give it a form. Set one of those into a shape that stands without your hand on it. Then it is held without being gripped, and the exchange stays open.
cells.sheetLine: You let go, and giving runs both ways now.
cells.place: releasing your grip on what the change left behind

cells.tense: You are bracing against a version of this that ended already and hasn't been told so.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: When you catch yourself reaching for a load that isn't yours, put it down unannounced and keep walking — no announcement, no accounting, no looking back at who picks it up.
cells.core:
You are still holding your end up in an exchange that has closed — counting what is owed, watching what comes back, ready in case it does not. The bracing has moved in before the facts. You are preparing for a shortfall in an account that has been settled, or one that was going to stay short however hard you held it.

A steadier grip will not save this. What holds under pressure here is putting the load down where it belongs, on your own side, and finding out that you do not collapse without it. Carry only your part, and treat the rest as belonging to whoever carries it. What you have held quietly weighs more than the watching did.
cells.sheetLine: You're still holding an exchange that already closed.
cells.place: releasing your grip on what the change left behind

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: sharpen the one skill by repeating its hardest part
cells.ask: Find the part of what you offer that still builds something in you, and repeat only that part, letting the rest go undone — then see what the space does.
cells.core:
You give to people and get nothing back, and you stopped expecting otherwise. The exchange runs one way and you show up anyway. That is not generosity now, it is a habit that outlasted the thing it was for. Fairness felt natural once, and you stand on the far side of it.

What is absent is not effort. It is the distinction between what is wanted and what you have persisted in offering. Sit with one evening's worth and sort the real from the carried-over. Cross out one line from the second column and leave the space open. Not as a loss — as the place where something wanted can land.
cells.sheetLine: You give, nothing comes back, and you stopped expecting it.
cells.place: releasing your grip on what the change left behind

cells.tense: You are already in the room where the fairness gets done, and you don't call it yours.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Before the next adjustment, hold their account and the one you already have side by side for one full breath, then move or don't — the knowing was yours either way.
cells.core:
In the group you are in, things come out even around you. You say the room just works, or the others are easy to work with. Fairness is being done — splits adjusted, credit put where it belongs, a share handed back quietly — and the doing has your hand in it. Call it chemistry if someone presses.

That part is not on the record. You know what is fair here before anyone says it, and treating that as nothing is how it stays off the books. Before the next adjustment, hold both accounts — the one being offered and the one you already have — for one breath. Then move or don't. Either way it is yours, precisely because you knew first.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness here is your work, and you shrug it off.
cells.place: releasing your grip on what the change left behind

attempts.check: The draft's weakest claim is that the person has something finished in hand that they are refusing to set down — the record gives the seat (purposeful release) and the balance, not evidence of a completed thing, so a reader could rightly say the letting-go is about something still living. If that's wrong the ask still holds: keeping hold of what the ending actually produced costs nothing even if the ending is still in progress, and it teaches the person something either way. The sentence that serves me rather than them is anything about doors behind them or ledgers — I've kept the seat's own language off the glass, but the pull to make release sound noble is the posture to watch. Cells written so the release is named as the setting-down, never as a verdict on what they released.
